**How the state is derived.** By the tag rule of the rustinfer repository's
[`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/docs/testing.md) (set in [#27](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/27)), a test
cites a requirement in its doc comment with exactly one of three tags: `Verifies RI-X-NNN: <part>`
only when the clause is fully implemented in the code, `Groundwork for RI-X-NNN: <part>` while it
is not, and `Reserved RI-X-NNN (R<n>)` for a test asserting a later-release refusal. A requirement is
<span class="state-ok">implemented</span> when it has at least one `Verifies` tag and no
`Groundwork for` tag; <span class="state-part">partial</span> when it has any `Groundwork for` tag;
<span class="state-no">reserved only</span> when it has only `Reserved` tags; and
<span class="state-no">planned</span> otherwise, with its release. The tags are read from the comments
of the integration tests under `crates/*/tests` and the `#[cfg(test)]` modules under `crates/*/src`;
an id mentioned without a tag word (prose, a `//!` module header) never counts. The *tags* column gives
the counts as Verifies / Groundwork for / Reserved and the *evidence* column the files, with the count
per file where it is more than one.

The Epic [#1](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/1) checklist's assignment of an id to an issue is shown in the evidence
column as information and does not change the state: 38 ids are assigned to a
closed issue, and 10 of them are not implemented by the tag rule
(RI-MIR-011, RI-MIR-012, RI-KC-008, RI-KC-011, RI-ART-005, RI-ART-012, RI-TGT-004, RI-RV-002, RI-WST-003, RI-WST-005). The SRS's own status field, in the *SRS status* column,
changes only when a release revises the document, so it is *Draft* for every requirement today
(by SRS status: Draft 188) and is not what the
[progress](progress.html) page counts: that page reads the *state* column of each component table
below, implemented as done, partial as progress, reserved only and planned as later. The tracker
state is read live from GitHub
(`data/progress-snapshot.json`, fetched 2026-11-14 03:14 UTC); the
[issues](issues.html) page computes its *SRS requirements implemented* headline from the same code.

| RI-MIR-001 | The Model IR SHALL be a typed SSA graph: each node applies one operator to named input tensors and defines named outputs; the graph SHALL be acyclic. *Rationale: One contract for every frontend and backend (ADR-005).* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> | 4 / 0 / 0 | Draft | Verifies: [`rustinfer-mir/tests/graph_validation.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/graph_validation.rs) ×4; Epic: closed [#3](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/3) |
| RI-MIR-002 | A shape SHALL be a list of dimensions, each a static integer or a named dynamic dimension from the set `batch`, `num_tokens`, `seq_len`, `beam`, bounded by the profile. *Rationale: Semi-static artifact (INV §0).* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> | 18 / 0 / 0 | Draft | Verifies: [`rustinfer-artifact/tests/profile.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-artifact/tests/profile.rs), [`rustinfer-mir/src/scan.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/src/scan.rs), [`rustinfer-mir/tests/boundary.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/boundary.rs), [`rustinfer-mir/tests/shapes.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/shapes.rs) ×15; Epic: closed [#3](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/3) |
| RI-MIR-003 | Dtypes SHALL be bf16, fp16, fp32, fp8 (OCP e4m3 per OCP-OFP8, FNUZ e4m3 per AMD-FNUZ), int8, int4x2, fp4x2, ue8m0, int32, int64, bool, each with a defined element size; quantized tensors SHALL carry a compression encoding (RI-MIR-011). `fp4x2` holds OCP MX E2M1 values (OCP-MX), two per byte: along the innermost axis, value 2i is the low nibble (bits 3..0) and value 2i+1 the high nibble (bits 7..4) of byte i. A nibble is a sign bit (bit 3), a 2-bit exponent with bias 1 and a 1-bit mantissa, exponent 0 being subnormal: codes 0x0 to 0x7 are 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 0x8 to 0xF their negatives (0x8 is −0); there is no Inf and no NaN. An `fp4x2` tensor's shape counts E2M1 values, its innermost axis SHALL be even, and it stores one byte per two values. `ue8m0` is the OCP MX v1.1 UE8M0 scale (E8M0 in v1.0): one unsigned byte e with value 2^(e−127) for e in 0 to 254 and NaN for e = 255; it has no sign, zero or Inf. Its IR token is `ue8m0`, after OCP MX v1.1: no Model IR reader has ever accepted `e8m0`, so the rename breaks no document, and `e8m0` is refused as an unknown dtype (checkpoint fields spelled `e8m0` are frontend input, RI-FE-006). *Rationale: The formats AMD matrix cores take; ADR-010 puts MXFP4 in R1. fp16 and fp32 are* | High | R1 (bf16, fp16, fp32, fp8, fp4x2, ue8m0, int32, int64, bool); R2 (int8); R3 (int4x2) | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> | 27 / 0 / 1 | Draft | Verifies: [`rustinfer-mir/src/dtype.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/src/dtype.rs) ×2, [`rustinfer-mir/tests/dtypes.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/dtypes.rs) ×7, [`rustinfer-mir/tests/mx.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/mx.rs) ×4, [`rustinfer-target/src/numeric.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-target/src/numeric.rs), [`rustinfer-target/tests/mx.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-target/tests/mx.rs) ×6, [`rustinfer-target/tests/numeric.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-target/tests/numeric.rs) ×7; Reserved: [`rustinfer-mir/tests/dtypes.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/dtypes.rs); Epic: closed [#3](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/3), [#34](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/34) |

## 3.2.5 Kernel compiler

| id | text | priority | release | state | tags | SRS status | evidence |

| RI-KC-001 | Kernels SHALL be written as Rust generators: functions taking a parameter struct (dtypes, tiles, layouts, pipeline depth, fused epilogue) and emitting Kernel IR through a builder; no kernel SHALL exist as MLIR text, HIP, OpenCL or assembly source except through a generator (RI-KC-009). *Rationale: ADR-005; the generator is the unit the autotuner explores.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-part">partly implemented</span> | 0 / 1 / 0 | Draft | Groundwork for: [`rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs); Epic: open [#9](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/9) (not started) |
| RI-KC-002 | The Kernel IR SHALL be an MLIR dialect at tile level with explicit layouts: tiles, memory spaces (global, shared, register), barriers, a matrix-multiply op, masked loads and stores, reductions, structured control flow; thread identity SHALL NOT appear. *Rationale: A tile IR retargets to SIMT, vector and mesh devices; a thread IR does not.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-ok">implemented</span> | 31 / 0 / 0 | Draft | Verifies: [`rustinfer-kc/src/mlir/lower.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/src/mlir/lower.rs) ×2, [`rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/builder.rs) ×13, [`rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs) ×9, [`rustinfer-kc/tests/mlir_link.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/mlir_link.rs) ×7; Epic: closed [#7](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/7) |
| RI-KC-003 | AMD lowering SHALL go through the MLIR `gpu` pipeline to `rocdl` and the LLVM AMDGPU back end, emitting MFMA for the matrix op with each architecture's formats (bf16; fp8 FNUZ (AMD-FNUZ) on gfx942; OCP fp8 (OCP-OFP8), fp4, fp6 with UE8M0 scales on gfx950), LDS for shared tiles, and bounds-checked buffer loads. For an `fp4x2` weight with the `mx` encoding, by default (`--activations bf16`, RI-CLI-002) on gfx950 and gfx942 the weights SHALL stay packed in device memory and each weight tile SHALL be dequantized to bf16 in the kernel (on gfx950 with the `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4` class of conversions; on gfx942, which has no FP4 format and no scaled MFMA, by integer and bf16 arithmetic), feeding the bf16 MFMA with bf16 activations, so gfx950, gfx942 and cpu compute the same W4A16 product. With `--activations mxfp8` or `mxfp4`, valid on gfx950 only, the matrix op SHALL lower to `llvm.amdgcn.mfma.scale.f32.16x16x128.f8f6f4` or `llvm.amdgcn.mfma.scale.f32.32x32x64.f8f6f4` (V_MFMA_SCALE_F32_*_F8F6F4) with the weight operand in E2M1 (format code 4) and its UE8M0 scale per 32 K-values, the bf16 activation tile being quantized in the kernel to E4M3 or E2M1 with a UE8M0 scale per 32 K-values by RI-MIR-012; the activation stays bf16 in memory. The activation format SHALL NOT depend on batch size, token count or bucket (RI-GC-004). Attention kernels SHALL dequantize fp8 and MXFP4 KV (RI-KVC-008) to bf16 in the kernel on both. fp6 is not an R1 format. *Rationale: The first target. The bf16 default follows vLLM, whose dense W4A16 MXFP4* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-part">partly implemented</span> | 0 / 1 / 0 | Draft | Groundwork for: [`rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-kc/tests/dialect.rs); Epic: open [#8](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/8) (in review 2026-11-13), [#38](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/38) (not started) |
| RI-KC-004 | RISC-V lowering SHALL be rustinfer's own: Kernel IR to a vector form (RVV with the matrix extensions where the core has them) through the LLVM RISC-V back end, and to a mesh form for Tensix-class devices through their open MLIR dialect; the SPIR-V path for Vulkan-class devices SHALL use MLIR's `spirv` dialect. *Rationale: No vendor kernel exists on RISC-V; the IR must be ours end to end. The vector form* | High | R2 (spirv, compile-tested); R3 (riscv-vector, compile-tested); R4 (riscv-mesh) | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | — |

A block's bytes per layer SHALL be block size × KV heads × 2 (K and V) × bytes per head, where bytes per head is head_dim × element size for bf16 and fp8, and head_dim / 2 + head_dim / 32 for MXFP4: the packed values, then the block's UE8M0 scales in the same block, so one block table addresses both. The pool size (RI-KVC-003) and the Plan geometry (RI-GC-006) SHALL use these bytes. | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-part">partly implemented</span> | 0 / 8 / 0 | Draft | Groundwork for: [`rustinfer-artifact/tests/kv_geometry.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-artifact/tests/kv_geometry.rs) ×5, [`rustinfer-artifact/tests/plan.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-artifact/tests/plan.rs), [`rustinfer-mir/tests/kv_dtypes.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/kv_dtypes.rs), [`rustinfer-target/tests/kv.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-target/tests/kv.rs); Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started), [#37](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/37) (in progress) |
| RI-KVC-002 | Allocation and release SHALL be O(1) from one pre-allocated pool with an LRU free list; no per-block heap allocation at run time. *Rationale: vLLM V1's block pool; prefix reuse must cost nothing at a 0 percent hit rate.* | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-no">planned R1</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |
| RI-KVC-003 | Pool size SHALL be the smaller of `free_gpu_memory_fraction` (default 0.9) and an explicit `max_tokens`, computed after weights and arena. | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-004 | A sequence longer than the profile's `max_seq_len` SHALL be refused at admission. | Critical | R1 | <span class="state-no">planned R1</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | Epic: open [#13](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/13) (not started) |
| RI-KVC-005 | Filled blocks SHALL be indexed in a radix tree keyed by (token prefix, KV group, LoRA id, multimodal item hashes, optional per-request `cache_salt`); a new request SHALL reuse matching blocks and skip their computation and SHALL NOT match a block whose key differs in any component; reuse SHALL be on by default; hits and misses SHALL be counted. *Rationale: SGLang's RadixAttention; agent traffic served well by default.* | High | R2 | <span class="state-no">planned R2</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-006 | Eviction SHALL be prioritised LRU with per-block priority (0 to 100, default 35) and optional retention windows; only unreferenced leaf blocks are evictable. | Medium | R3 | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-007 | Evicted blocks MAY be offloaded to host DRAM, CXL memory or NVMe tiers under the planner's KV policy and restored on reuse. | Medium | R3 (DRAM, NVMe); R4 (CXL, remote) | <span class="state-no">planned R3</span> | 0 / 0 / 0 | Draft | — |
| RI-KVC-008 | FP8 and INT8 cache storage with per-block scales SHALL be supported where the catalog's attention kernels read them. In R1 the KV storage dtype is selected by `--kv-dtype` (RI-CLI-002): `bf16` (default); `fp8`, OCP E4M3 (OCP-OFP8) on gfx950 and cpu and FNUZ E4M3 (AMD-FNUZ) on gfx942, with one fp32 scale per layer for K and one for V, taken from the checkpoint's KV scales when it has them (RI-FE-006) and 1.0 otherwise, recorded in the Plan; `mxfp4`, K and V each stored as `fp4x2` with the `mx` encoding in blocks of 32 along `head_dim` per token and head, the UE8M0 scale of each block computed by the cache-write kernel under RI-MIR-012. A `head_dim` not a multiple of 32 with `mxfp4` SHALL be refused naming the KV group. Accuracy caveat, stated in this clause, the `--kv-dtype` help text and `docs/entry-points.md`: FP8 E4M3 is the industry's KV format; FP4 KV has shipped only as NVFP4, and NVIDIA measured Llama-3.3-70B MMLU at about 81.9 percent with NVFP4 KV and about 77.8 percent with MXFP4 KV (NV-KV). MXFP4 KV is a normal selectable dtype with no build-time gate (ADR-010). *Rationale: ADR-010: the owner's decision to ship MXFP4 KV in R1 with its caveat* | High | R1 (bf16, fp8 per-tensor scale, mxfp4); R2 (int8, fp8 per-block scales) | <span class="state-part">partly implemented</span> | 0 / 13 / 0 | Draft | Groundwork for: [`rustinfer-artifact/tests/kv_geometry.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-artifact/tests/kv_geometry.rs) ×3, [`rustinfer-cli/tests/cli.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-cli/tests/cli.rs) ×2, [`rustinfer-core/tests/kv_dtype.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-core/tests/kv_dtype.rs), [`rustinfer-mir/tests/kv_dtypes.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-mir/tests/kv_dtypes.rs) ×3, [`rustinfer-target/tests/kv.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-target/tests/kv.rs) ×4; Epic: open [#37](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/37) (in progress) |

| RI-WST-005 | Sluice SHALL verify dtype, shape and byte range of every tensor against the shard header before reading it and SHALL refuse the first mismatch naming the tensor; with `--verify-weights` it SHALL also check each tensor's bytes against the SHA-256 recorded in the manifest (RI-ART-005) and refuse the first mismatch, or the first tensor with no recorded digest, naming the tensor. *Rationale: The shard header is the SAFETENSORS header; the digest is FIPS-180-4 SHA-256.* | High | R1 | <span class="state-part">partly implemented</span> | 3 / 13 / 0 | Draft | Verifies: [`rustinfer-sluice/tests/verify.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-sluice/tests/verify.rs) ×3; Groundwork for: [`rustinfer-sluice/tests/mxfp4.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-sluice/tests/mxfp4.rs) ×4, [`rustinfer-sluice/tests/refusal.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-sluice/tests/refusal.rs) ×5, [`rustinfer-sluice/tests/verify.rs`](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/blob/main/crates/rustinfer-sluice/tests/verify.rs) ×4; Epic: closed [#18](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/18), [#39](https://github.com/itej89/rustinfer/issues/39) |
